The Moon’s azimuth of **333°** indicates the direction it would be in if it were above the horizon—roughly northwest—but it would not be visible until it rose.

At that time, the Sun was also well below the horizon, so daylight glare was not the issue; the Moon’s position below the horizon was decisive.
